ambiguities.aspect: clk_div output latency / registered vs combinational
readings: clk_div is the direct logical OR of the two intermediate registers, so it changes in the same half-cycle in which the counter reaches the step boundary
clk_div is itself registered (on clk or on the combining edge), so every transition of the intermediate clocks appears one half source-clock cycle later on clk_div
ambiguities.note: Both satisfy 'the two intermediate clocks are OR-ed' but produce edges offset by half a clk cycle.

ambiguities.aspect: Distribution of the 3 high half-steps between the posedge and negedge intermediate clocks
readings: posedge-domain pulse is high for half-steps 0-1 and the negedge-domain pulse for half-step 2, so the OR is high for exactly half-steps 0-2 (1.5 clk high / 2.0 clk low)
posedge-domain pulse is high for half-steps 0-2 and the negedge-domain pulse also covers half-step 3, so the OR is high for 4 half-steps (2.0 clk high / 1.5 clk low)
ambiguities.note: 'high for the first 3 half clock steps' fixes the total high time but not which branch (and hence which edge) supplies which step; the described 'duty cycle imbalance adjustment' can be read either way.

ambiguities.aspect: Initial/post-reset state and phase of the first output period
readings: All state is 0 after reset and counting starts immediately, so clk_div rises in the first half-step after reset release (first period begins with a high phase)
The first posedge-derived pulse is only generated when the counter reaches its terminal value, so clk_div stays low for the whole first period and the high phase begins after the first wrap
ambiguities.note: Spec only says reset initializes counter and intermediate clocks to 0; the resulting first-period phase is unspecified.

readings: Counter is 3 bits counting 0..6 and wraps on cnt == MUL2_DIV_CLK-1 (7 states = 7 half-steps = 3.5 clk)
Counter wraps on cnt == MUL2_DIV_CLK (i.e., 0..7, 8 half-steps = 4.0 clk), with the 7th step unused or used as the phase-shift slot
ambiguities.note: MUL2_DIV_CLK = 7 is described as both the number of half-steps and the counter modulus; whether it is used as a terminal value or as an exclusive modulus changes the division ratio.
